content_voiceover: This flowchart lays out the design of E1910, the randomized phase three trial that established blinatumomab as consolidation therapy in MRD negative B-ALL, again flagged as a new indication. Patients first receive induction chemotherapy for two cycles, and if they don't achieve complete remission or CRi they're discontinued from the study. Those who respond move to one cycle of intensification chemotherapy, and if their MRD becomes negative, defined as less than point zero one percent, they're randomized. The blinatumomab arm receives two cycles of blinatumomab with a two week rest between cycles, followed by four cycles of consolidation chemotherapy interspersed with two more cycles of blinatumomab, then blood or marrow transplant if a suitable donor exists, and maintenance chemotherapy continuing for two and a half years from the start of intensification. The control arm skips blinatumomab entirely, going straight from randomization to four cycles of standard consolidation chemotherapy, then transplant if eligible, then the same maintenance schedule. The trial enrolled four hundred eighty eight patients with a median age of fifty one, and two hundred twenty four who achieved MRD negative CR were randomized one to one across sites in the US, Canada, and Israel, with about twenty percent in each arm proceeding to autologous transplant. This is the study design slide, the actual survival results supporting the new indication appear on the next slide.
keypoints: E1910: phase 3, blinatumomab vs SOC consolidation in MRD-negative CR
Design: induction -> intensification -> randomize if MRD <0.01%
Blina arm: 2 cycles blina + 4 cycles chemo + 2 more blina cycles
488 enrolled, 224 MRD-negative CR randomized 1:1, new indication
keypoint_voiceover: E1910 randomized MRD negative B-ALL patients after induction and intensification chemotherapy to receive blinatumomab woven into consolidation versus standard consolidation alone, followed by transplant if eligible and two and a half years of maintenance, this design is what supports blinatumomab's newest frontline consolidation indication.
